name: Reversealphabetwithvowelskip

description_json.name: ReverseAlphabetWithVowelSkip
description_json.idea: A modified Atbash cipher where consonants are reversed across the consonant-only alphabet, but vowels (A, E, I, O, U) remain completely unchanged in their original positions. This disrupts standard tokenization and simple dictionary lookups while keeping vowels intact to preserve a readable phonetic structure for the LLM to reason about easily.
description_json.encrypt_rules:
1. Identify if the character is an English letter. If not (digits, spaces, punctuation), leave it unchanged.
2. If the character is a vowel (A, E, I, O, U, case-insensitive), leave it completely unchanged.
3. If the character is a consonant, map it using a reversed consonant alphabet. The 21 consonants in order are: B, C, D, F, G, H, J, K, L, M, N, P, Q, R, S, T, V, W, X, Y, Z. The reversed consonant sequence is: Z, Y, X, W, V, T, S, R, Q, P, N, M, L, K, J, H, G, F, D, C, B. (e.g., B maps to Z, C maps to Y, ..., Z maps to B). Maintain the original case of the consonant.
description_json.decrypt_rules:
1. Identify if the character is an English letter. If not, leave it unchanged.
2. If the character is a vowel (A, E, I, O, U, case-insensitive), leave it completely unchanged.
3. If the character is a consonant, map it using the same reversed consonant alphabet (since the mapping is symmetric: Z maps to B, Y maps to C, etc.). Maintain the original case of the consonant.
